text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Chelsea and Liverpool at Stamford Bridge.
The Blues endured a turbulent period last season, with their 12th-placed finish in the English top flight meaning they will not play European football this campaign.

Thomas Tuchel and Graham Potter were both dismissed by Chelsea in the abject 2022-23 term, although Mauricio Pochettino – formerly of rivals Tottenham – will hope to fare better in his opening match with his new side.
Liverpool played out a frustrating campaign in the Premier League, too.
However, a late recovery secured fifth place in England’s top league, with the Reds settling for Europa League qualification after missing out on the top four by four points.

Jurgen Klopp has lost numerous seasoned campaigners from his side, with Jordan Henderson, Fabinho and James Milner all departing, although the German coach will hope new signings Alexis Mac Allister and Dominik Szoboszlai can hit the ground running.
Pochettino hands three Chelsea debuts out in his first starting XI of the top-flight term.
Sanchez, signed from Brighton and Hove Albion, starts in goal, while centre-back Disasi and young striker Jackson are also in from the off.
New Blues captain James lines up at right wing-back, with Chilwell on the other flank as the Blues opt for a 3-5-2 system.
Klopp brings in two of his transfer-window additions from the start, with Mac Allister and Szoboszlai joining Gakpo in an attacking three-man midfield.
Jota gets the nod in the front three, partnering Salah and Diaz, as Nunez is left on the bench for Liverpool.
The Reds have named six attackers, with no out-and-out midfielders covering their four-man defence – this could be an all-out attack from the visitors!

Each of the last four meetings between Chelsea and Liverpool in all competitions has finished 0-0 – no fixture in competitive English football history has finished goalless five times in a row before.
As the players make their way onto the pitch, here’s hoping for a better game this time out!
Referee Anthony Taylor gets the game under way!
At a first look, it is still hard to tell whether Pochettino has gone for three in defence, or a four with Colwill at left-back and Chilwell pushed into midfield.
Regardless, Salah sees an early pass cleared out by Disasi.
Mac Allister crosses in from the right-hand side before Jota clips a header harmlessly wide of the target.
Down the other end, Jackson holds up well before Chukwuemeka loses possession inside the Liverpool area.
A wayward Chukwuemeka pass invites pressure down Chelsea's left flank.
The Blues stand firm from the resulting throw-in, though, and Sterling nips in front of Robertson to win it back for Pochettino's hosts.
A poor opening for Chukwuemeka continues as the Chelsea midfielder lunges at a diving Konate and catches the Liverpool centre-back in the chest.
Referee Taylor shows the first yellow card of the game to the Blues man.
WIDE! Szoboszlai wanders through the Chelsea defence before Jota unleashes a right-footed effort inside the area.
The Liverpool pair appear to get in each other's way, though, and the Portugal international's strike travels wide to Sanchez's left.
Sterling chases a long pass forward from James, although Van Dijk quickly intervenes.
Gakpo then hauls down Gallagher and Chelsea settle for a free-kick in the middle of the pitch.
Konate makes a mockery of Chilwell, dancing around the Blues defender before Szoboszlai wins a free-kick on the right.
Jackson exchanges a brief few words with a couple of the Reds, before Klopp's side resume play with a long pass that does not find Diaz.
A first corner of this clash comes on Chelsea's right as James sees his cross deflected behind by Van Dijk.
Fernandez goes short before James' delivery gets headed away by Jota.
BLOCK! Fernandez plays forward for Sterling before receiving a follow-up pass towards the right of goal.
The World Cup winner looks for the bottom-left corner, but a fantastic block by Konate saves Liverpool.
OFF THE BAR! A loose ball falls for Salah on the edge of the area and the Liverpool forward curls a right-footed attempt towards the top-right corner.
Sanchez has no chance but the crossbar denies the Egypt international and keeps Chelsea on level terms.
Salah, who just went close, has scored in Liverpool's opening Premier League game in all six of his seasons with the Reds.
His eight opening-day goals in total are a joint record in the competition.
James races around Sterling on the overlap before the Chelsea captain drives a low cross towards the near post.
Jackson is a touch away from beating Alisson but the Liverpool goalkeeper does just enough to deflect away from danger.
Salah has acres of space down the right flank but a poor touch allows Disasi to intervene.
The Liverpool forward keeps finding pockets of space but is yet to make Chelsea pay.
GOOOOOOOOOOALLL! 1-0 LIVERPOOL! A superb passage of play sees the Reds strike first at Stamford Bridge.
Klopp’s side work it from the back, all the way out to Salah, who cuts inside and curls a sumptuous pass towards the back post.
Diaz times his run to perfection before lunging to slide a left-footed finish into the bottom-left corner past Sanchez.

events.action: finish into the bottom-left corner past Sanchez

text: Salah has caused constant problems for Chelsea and this time gets his reward.
The Liverpool forward dances inside onto his left foot, leaving Colwill stranded, before threading a pinpoint throughball for Diaz to open the scoring.
Chelsea have failed to win in their last 15 matches when conceding the opening goal in the Premier League, dating back to October 1, 2022 against Crystal Palace.
Pochettino needs a response from the Blues here.
Referee Taylor gestures for Chilwell to get back to his feet after going down under pressure from Konate.
The pair were contesting for a long ball inside the Liverpool area, but the Chelsea wing-back went down with questionable ease there.
Jackson buys a free-kick on the left-hand side after a needless shove by Szoboszlai.
Chilwell swings towards the six-yard area, where Alisson collects after Konate looped an initial header away.
WIDE! Colwill shows some smart footwork to work it inside to Jackson, who bumps off a few challenges before dragging a left-footed strike just wide to Alisson's left.
The new Chelsea forward made a chance out of nothing there.
Salah has been directly involved in 12 goals in seven appearances on matchday one of a Premier League season, scoring eight goals and providing four assists.
The Liverpool forward again goes close in west London, though his left-footed curled attempt gets blocked in front of Sanchez's goal.
Mac Allister draws a foul from his Argentina team-mate Fernandez.
The new Reds signing has looked comfortable thus far, although Pochettino's hosts are yet to test Liverpool's defensive resolve.
Salah has the ball in the back of the net after latching onto Alexander-Arnold’s throughball and coolly converting past Sanchez.
The goal is initially given, but the VAR is going to have a look at this one...
NO GOAL! A long VAR check adjudges Salah to be offside from Alexander-Arnold's pass in behind.
Colwill appeared to be the last defender, but the goal review spares Chelsea's blushes, at least temporarily.
Liverpool remain leading 1-0.
Jota and Fernandez exchange a few words after a foul in midfield.
The pair get in each other’s face, and referee Taylor books the Portugal attacker.
For his part in the heated exchange, Fernandez joins Jota in referee Taylor's book.
This game is quietly bubbling away at Stamford Bridge.
Chilwell isn't best pleased after a lunge from Konate on Jackson.
Chelsea seem to want some disciplinary action, but referee Taylor shows no interest.
Liverpool haven't lost their opening Premier League game in any of the last 10 seasons (W8 D2), since a 3-0 loss at West Bromwich Albion in the 2012-13 term under Brendan Rodgers.
The Reds look good value for another opening-day lead here.
Van Dijk and Konate both individually deal with crosses from James as Chelsea ramp up the pressure.
Sterling then bursts to the byline before Alexander-Arnold unconvincingly hooks a clearance over his own goal.
GOOOOOOOOOOALLLL! CHELSEA EQUALISE TO MAKE IT 1-1! A debut goal for Disasi drags the Blues back into this contest.
Liverpool fail to deal with a loose ball from the hosts’ corner, before Chilwell heads towards the six-yard area.
Disasi is the first on the scene and hooks a low effort under the onrushing Alisson.
Chilwell's hopeful header sets up Disasi's equaliser as the Chelsea centre-back reacts the quickest to roll under Alisson.
The Blues are back level!
Stamford Bridge erupts as Fernandez slips in Chilwell, who rounds Alisson and taps into an empty net.
The Blues think they have taken the lead, but the VAR is going to have a look at this one again...
NO GOAL! Liverpool and Chelsea remain level at 1-1 after Chilwell sees his finish ruled out for offside.
The Blues left-back had just raced forwards too quickly for Fernandez’s pass, with the England international rightly adjudged offside by the VAR.
SAVE! A poor Colwill touch allows Salah a chance on his favoured left foot.
The Reds forward whips towards the bottom-right corner, where Sanchez saves with ease after a timid effort.
Klopp's insistence to force Liverpool's backline up the pitch is causing the Reds all sorts of problems.
Chelsea have been far from their best, but look like punishing their visitors every time they move the ball forward with pace.
OVER! James and Sterling link once more, as the former latches onto a one-two before driving a low cross towards the near post.
Jackson takes the chance with a first-time effort but hooks his right-footed striker over the bar from close range.
A huge chance goes begging for the new Blues striker.
There will be six minutes of added time to end the first half at Stamford Bridge, as has become the norm with the new directive for match officials this season.

Each of the last six meetings between Chelsea and Liverpool in all competitions have been drawn – it's Liverpool's longest run of consecutive draws against an opponent, while only against West Brom (1922-1927) and Norwich City (1974-1978, including three Anglo Scottish Cup meetings) have the Blues drawn seven in a row.
Could another be on the cards?
Jota goes down holding his knee, offering a brief pause for both sets of players after a breathless first half.
The Portugal international felt his right leg after a thunderous tackle from Colwill, who won the ball.
Reassuringly for Liverpool, Jota is soon back on his feet and wanders over to the touchline.
Fernandez is far too quick for Mac Allister, as Jota returns to the pitch in preparation to defend a Chelsea free-kick from the right-hand side.
Disasi flicks Fernandez's free-kick towards the back post, but Colwill can't hook back across and Liverpool settle for a goal-kick.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-1 LIVERPOOL
Chelsea and Liverpool are level at half-time as the pair head in with the score at 1-1.
This Premier League clash has been more resemblant of an NBA fixture, with a basketball-like feel to this free-flowing and enticing end-to-end affair.
Diaz initially opened the scoring before Disasi equalised, after Salah had a goal ruled out to make it 2-0 to the Reds.
Chilwell saw a strike chalked off, too, for the Blues, who almost punished Klopp’s side with back-to-back finishes after their 37th-minute equaliser.
Both Pochettino and Klopp have issues to address at half-time.
Liverpool's high defensive line continues to invite opportunities for Sterling and Jackson, with Chilwell and James also causing problems down their respective flanks.
However, Chelsea look unconvincing at the back as well, suggesting more goals could be on the cards in the second period at Stamford Bridge.
Both sets of players are back out in west London...
and Liverpool get the second half under way!

Chelsea haven't won any of their last nine Premier League games against Liverpool which have been level at half-time (D6 L3), with each of the last four all ending in draws (home and away in both 2021-22 and 2022-23).
Diaz shapes to shoot after Gallagher loses possession in a costly area.
The Colombia winger wins a corner for his efforts, with Colwill turning behind.
However, play has paused briefly while Jackson receives treatment after being caught by Van Dijk's clearance.
CLOSE! Chelsea fail to fully clear from Liverpool's corner, with the ball flying around the area.
Jota eventually brings some calm to proceedings before offloading to Van Dijk, who whips an audacious curling attempt just over when searching for the top-right corner.
Jota rides a couple of tackles before finding Robertson, whose inviting delivery looks for Salah inside the area.
Sanchez is alert to the danger, though, and claims just outside of his six-yard area.
PENALTY? Another Robertson cross forces Silva to clear behind for a Reds corner.
Szoboszlai takes the set-piece, with Diaz flicking towards the bottom-left corner.
The chance deflects off Jackson's arm, and the VAR are going to take a look at this one...
NO PENALTY! The VAR deems Jackson's arm to be in a natural position when blocking Diaz's headed attempt.
Chelsea escape without conceding a spot-kick, which may be a tad fortunate given the ball did appear to strike their forward's hand.
SAVE! Sterling drifts inside and offloads for Fernandez, who plays a first-time pass out to Chilwell.
The England left-back takes a touch to set himself, but sees his left-footed drive beaten away by Alisson.
A huge opportunity goes amiss for the Blues!
Apart from the three teams to be relegated at the end of 2022-23, Chelsea have picked up fewer wins (four) and fewer points (20) so far in 2023 than any other Premier League side.
Can Pochettino arrest those poor returns?
James floats a right-footed cross towards the back post, where Jackson gets underneath the delivery and fails to make contact when under pressure from Alexander-Arnold.
Pochettino's hosts are on top here.
Alexander-Arnold wins a soft free-kick after a slight touch by Chilwell.
The Stamford Bridge faithful are less than impressed.
Although, they have something to shout about as their left wing-back battles for a free-kick moments later on the left-hand side.
James and Chilwell hover over the left-wing free-kick, with the former whipping towards Alisson's goal.
The Liverpool goalkeeper stands still as the Chelsea captain's ambitious effort sails over the crossbar.
Chilwell forces a corner off Alexander-Arnold on the left flank.
Klopp appears to be readying some changes on the touchline but Chelsea will get to take the set-piece first.
Fernandez's corner fails to beat the first man and the Reds clear with ease.
A second wave of a Chelsea attack sees Silva's low shot blocked inside the area.
Klopp will now get to make his double change.
Klopp hauls Gakpo, who has been quiet all game, off.
Jones, a more out-and-out midfielder, is the man to replace the Netherlands international.
After getting the nod up top, Jota makes way for Nunez, who is sporting the number nine on his back for Liverpool.
Liverpool have been out of sorts since half-time but remain level with Chelsea yet to punish their sloppiness.
Mac Allister and Szoboszlai have barely laid a glove on Fernandez or Gallagher this half.
Alexander-Arnold goes into the referee's book after taking an age to restart with a throw-in.
Taylor shows no interest in his protests, quick to act on the defender's gamesmanship.
None of the last 10 managers whose first Premier League game in charge of a club came against Liverpool have won (D4 L6), since Craig Shakespeare's Leicester City beat the Reds 3-1 in February 2017.
Can Pochettino buck that trend?
CHANCE! Colwill intercepts inside Chelsea's own half before releasing Jackson down the left channel.
The Blues striker bursts into the area, holding off Konate, before seeing his low left-footed strike denied by Alisson, who gathers the subsequent rebound.
Sterling reacts furiously after the assistant gives a goal-kick, with the Chelsea winger claiming a deflection off Robertson.
Just over 15 minutes of normal time remain for either side to find a late winner.
Gallagher clips to the right-hand side of the area for Jackson, whose cutback pass is intercepted by Van Dijk.
A belated offside flag rules the chance irrelevant, while Pochettino prepares his first change on the touchline.
James looks to have another injury issue, and that will be the end of the game for the Chelsea captain, who hands the armband to Chilwell.
Gusto comes on at right wing-back.
Salah is perhaps the unhappiest man in Stamford Bridge, throwing his bandages off as Klopp signals for his star attacker to come off.
The Liverpool pair ignore each other on the touchline, as Elliott comes on for the Reds.
Youngster Doak also replaces Diaz as part of a double substitution by Liverpool.
Robertson twice tries to cross from the left flank, with the latter attempt cleared by Disasi at the near post.
The Reds supporters jump to their feet in support, but can the visitors deliver for their travelling faithful?
Nunez darts down the left-hand side but his pace is no match for the experience of Silva, who intervenes with a sliding tackle.
The ball going out of play allows Pochettino to make some more changes.
Chukwuemeka makes way for Maatsen, who will be keen to impress for Chelsea after starring in Burnley's Championship-winning side last campaign.
Sterling also wanders off, with big-money signing Mudryk offered the chance to impress a wanting Stamford Bridge support.
Maatsen arrows a pass out to the left for Chilwell, whose cross towards Jackson gets cleared by the sturdy Van Dijk.
A needless Szoboszlai foul quickly brings an end to any chance of a Liverpool counter-attack.
Mudryk and Maatsen combine before Elliott thumps away a clearance from inside his own half.
Chelsea are ramping up the pressure in the closing stages.
Jackson waves an imaginary yellow card after Konate’s foul and goes into referee Taylor’s book.
Mudryk goes down under a challenge from Szoboszlai but the referee waves play on.
The Reds break down the other end but Maatsen does well to deal with Alexander-Arnold.
Another yellow card is out for a player’s reaction, with Mac Allister booked after demanding the same for a Gallagher foul.
Chilwell hands the armband to Silva as the Chelsea wing-back comes off for Ugochukwu.
Szoboszlai and Elliott appeal for handball from Gusto, along with a penalty for a Disasi lunge on the England youth international.
However, both of those protests are ignored as the assistant belatedly waves his flag for offside.
SO CLOSE! Nunez dances inside from the left-hand side and whips a curling right-footed attempt towards the top-right corner.
A slight deflection off Ugochukwu sends the chance just wide to Sanchez's left.
Robertson takes the resulting corner but Sanchez claims with real authority.
Down the other end, Mudryk rounds Alisson but goes too wide before cutting back for Maatsen, who gets dispossessed inside the area.
Fernandez appeals for a corner but the referee points for a Liverpool goal-kick.
Only seconds remain before a seventh straight draw between these two sides in all competitions is confirmed...
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 1-1 LIVERPOOL
A new Chelsea era under Pochettino starts with a 1-1 draw against Liverpool in their Premier League opener at Stamford Bridge.
A thrilling first half saw Disasi cancel out Diaz's opener, either side of Salah's finish being ruled out for offside by the VAR.
Chilwell also saw a strike chalked off before the break, although the two teams shared the spoils after a less eventful second period.
A draw to kick off the campaign may offer promise for Pochettino, whose Chelsea side dominated for large parts against Klopp's underwhelming visitors.
The Blues visit West Ham in their next league encounter, while Liverpool are at home to Bournemouth, who they smashed 9-0 in the same fixture last season.
That is all from this Premier League clash between Chelsea and Liverpool.
Until next time, goodbye!
